newsitem.title: UK: Bradford wool market sees dull, hand-to-mouth trade.
newsitem.headline: Bradford wool market sees dull, hand-to-mouth trade.

text.p: Higher raw merino prices at Wednesday's wool auction in Australia spurred a limited amount of fresh enquiry at the Bradford tops market, local sources said.
Fine merino-based tops were quoted up two to three pence but traders said there were few firm trades and most involved hand-to-mouth purchases.
Some topmakers said customer call for deliveries of previously-placed orders had picked up again after a brief lull but others said demand was still slow.
One source expressed a common theme among exporters. "Sterling's strength is making new business difficult to the point of impossible," he said.

"Buyers have no need to rush into the market-place at the moment because raw wool prices are unlikely to rise at anything other than a slow pace," an industry analyst said. Most tops prices were quoted unchanged with only 58s English following finest tops up two pence after a slightly firmer UK raw wool market. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
